correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundary n=1 are explicit. For nonprimitive Dyck words an early zero-height separator disconnects crossing graphs. FIFO attains sum_j(h_j−1) and contains an opener-order Hamilton path for primitive words. Removing an interior adjacent UD and splitting the earliest-ending active chord yields a crossing tree by endpoint case analysis. Swapping inverted opener assignments at consecutive closes creates exactly one new crossing and preserves connectedness; bubble sorting gives every integer. Direct exhaustive matching enumeration through n=6 and all primitive constructive paths through n=10 independently corroborate, but do not replace, the induction.

originality.rationale: Comparison by mathematical implication: Gross–Šarković fix genus and prove Markov-chain mixing, not fixed left endpoints or exact crossing-count support; Chen et al. fix endpoint sets but prove symmetry of maxima of crossing/nesting patterns, not graph connectedness and count support; Pilaud–Rué count connected diagrams summed over all opening sets and supply the universal lower bound n-1, but do not provide the fixed-word sharp upper bound or connected interpolation. The proposed theorem has different quantifiers and adds a constructive exact support interval. Published-result search found no equivalent or stronger covering claim; historical priority is provisional, not established by absence from a database.
residual_risks: Historical priority remains provisional: other unpublished, unindexed, differently phrased or inaccessible results may cover the exact fixed-opening support theorem.
Published-result semantic search cannot establish global uniqueness or rule out stronger historical statements.

value.rationale: Connectivity of a chord-intersection graph is a global combinatorial constraint. The theorem characterizes feasibility by Dyck primitivity and gives a sharp no-gap exact crossing support for an infinite set of opener patterns. Nontrivial constructive tree and Hamilton-path endpoints, with a connectedness-preserving monotone swap algorithm, offer reusable structural insight beyond an isolated finite example or prior global counts.
